about.title: Personal Injury Help in Lindsay, California
about.longDescription: Lindsay is a tight-knit Tulare County community, but like any town with regular traffic on Rt 65, Hermosa, Tulare Road, and Mirage Avenue, collisions happen. Public records show 22 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with 33 people hurt — a reminder that everyday drives here carry real risk. Many of these crashes cluster around Friday afternoons, when commuters, farmworkers, and families are all moving through town at once. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, or in a fall, workplace accident, or other mishap, sorting out medical bills and insurance calls while healing is overwhelming. LawProactive is not a law firm — we're a free service that listens to what happened and connects you with an independent personal injury attorney in our network who can evaluate your situation. There's no cost to you for this connection, and the attorneys we work with take cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless they recover money for you. You focus on getting better; let someone who knows the local roads and California law help sort out the rest.

whyChoose.title: Why Connect With an Attorney Through LawProactive

items.title: You Have Two Years — But Don't Wait
items.desc: California law generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Acting sooner preserves evidence and options.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Clear-Cut
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Ordinary personal injury cases in California don't limit non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or emotional distress. An attorney can help you understand what your specific losses may be worth.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you pay nothing upfront and owe no attorney fee unless they win compensation for you. This lets you get help without added financial pressure.

items.question: How much does it cost to connect with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and there's no cost to you for being connected with an independent attorney. If you decide to hire that attorney, they typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice. We simply connect injured people in Lindsay and throughout Tulare County with independent attorneys who can evaluate their case.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: In most personal injury cases, California allows two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your injury involves a government entity, such as a city or county vehicle, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Lindsay?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Rt 65, Hermosa, Tulare Road, and Mirage Avenue are among the higher-volume corridors for reported injury collisions in Lindsay, with activity often clustering on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply publicly reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some blame for what happened. Any award would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it wouldn't bar you from recovering altogether.
